title: Immutability patterns: spread, structuredClone, and tradeoffs
hook: Immutability in JavaScript means copying and replacing — spread for shallow updates, structuredClone for deep copies, and awareness that const does not freeze nested objects. React state and Redux rely on reference change detection.

blocks.text: **Shallow copy**: spread `{ ...obj }`, `[...arr]`, `Object.assign` — nested objects still aliased. **structuredClone** deep-copies most built-ins including Date, Map, circular refs (not functions/prototypes). **Object.freeze** shallow immutability. **Immutable update** returns new root with changed branch — React setState pattern.

entries.plainDefinition: Built-in deep clone for structured data.
Reuse unchanged subtrees in new immutable tree.

blocks.text: React memo and useEffect deps compare by reference — mutating state in place skips updates. Time-travel debugging needs immutable history. C# records give value semantics; JS requires discipline or Immer.

blocks.title: JSON clone limits
blocks.body: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) drops undefined, functions, Date becomes string, no circular refs — prefer structuredClone when available.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Copy root
items.body: Spread object or array at top level.

items.title: Copy path to leaf
items.body: Spread each nested level along update path.

items.title: Set new value
items.body: Replace leaf; keep other branches shared.

diagram.title: Shallow vs deep
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  ROOT[Root object copy] --> N1[Nested ref A — shared if shallow]
  ROOT --> N2[Nested ref B — new if updated path]
  DEEP[structuredClone] --> ALL[All levels copied]

snippet.label: Shallow spread update
snippet.explanation: Each level along path copied; unrelated branches share references with original.

snippet.label: structuredClone deep
snippet.explanation: structuredClone handles Date, Map, circular refs — JSON clone cannot.

snippet.label: Array immutable ops
snippet.explanation: Spread, filter, map return new arrays — do not mutate source.

snippet.label: Failure mode — shallow trap
snippet.explanation: Spread only copies top level — nested mutation leaks between clones.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Spread thinking it deep-clones. Mutating state in React. JSON clone for Date/Map/circular. Object.freeze on nested tree — inner still mutable. Sort/reverse in place on shared array reference.

blocks.text: **Immer** uses Proxy drafts — ergonomic immutable updates in Redux Toolkit. **Persistent data structures** (Immutable.js) trade memory for sharing — less common now. **structuredClone** cannot clone functions or DOM nodes. Know **slice vs splice** — splice mutates. **Object.freeze** + **seal** + **preventExtensions** levels. Performance: shallow spread cheaper than deep clone every render — update only changed paths.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Says spread deep clones. Mutates array with sort() on state prop. Unaware structuredClone vs JSON differences.

interviewTakeaways: structuredClone for deep copy including Date, Map, cycles.
JSON clone loses types and functions.
Immutable update: copy path, replace root reference.
60s: Shallow vs deep. React reference equality. structuredClone limits. Immer pattern.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "const state means immutable." Strong: "const locks binding; nested objects still mutable — copy on update."
Weak: "JSON.stringify clone is enough." Strong: "Loses undefined, functions, Date; no cycles — use structuredClone."
Strong: "Show b.nested mutation affecting a after shallow spread."

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS Readonly<T> and readonly modifiers are compile-time only — run time still mutable without freeze.
C# record with with expression for non-destructive update; JS uses spread or Immer.
